coverage_note: Building permits issued by Alachua County (Growth Management) — the county's own permitting jurisdiction, chiefly unincorporated Alachua County and county-served areas. The City of Gainesville and Alachua County's other municipalities issue their own permits separately and are not in this feed; totals here are county-issued totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one Permit number in Alachua County's BuildingPermitsCS layer. The layer's grain is one row per permit: no collapsing applies or is needed.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Scoped trailing-12-month window (IssueDate >= 2025-11-18, IssueDate <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, administrative types excluded — see pull_where_extra), measured 2026-11-18 against the live layer: 8,702 rows = 8,702 distinct Permit, 0 duplicates. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: FULLADDR, the street address as published (present on 8,744 of 8,796 unscoped window permits). The layer publishes NO city and NO ZIP field: both carry as NULL, never inferred or derived.
field_map.application_date: ApplicationDate (epoch ms in the ArcGIS feed, converted to the civil date).
field_map.category: The layer publishes no residential/commercial class for a permit (Sub_Type lot classes are not a building class) — category stays NULL (the Boston treatment).
field_map.contractor_rule: LicensedContractorName ONLY — the county's published licensed contractor of record (present on 640 of 8,702 scoped window permits; 50 sampled at audit — all businesses: INC/LLC firms and national builders). ApplicantCompanyName is NEVER carried: despite its name it mixes businesses with individual applicants (audit samples include plain person names). ApplicanName (the applicant person name) and OwnerName (the property owner) are excluded from the pull's column list entirely and never requested.
field_map.issue_date: IssueDate (epoch ms, converted). The window is defined on it, bounded at both ends: the trailing 12 months ending at pull time (IssueDate <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in pull_where_extra). Two legacy closed permits carry junk future issue dates in the source (2029-03-30 and 2049-06-20, on old-style permit numbers 72820 and 79861); they fall outside the window's end by definition, are named here and on the Data Sources page, and are the only window-adjacent records so excluded (measured 2026-11-18: exactly 2 rows with IssueDate after 2026-11-18 in the whole layer window).
field_map.permit_number: Permit — verified exactly unique in the scoped window (8,702 distinct = 8,702 rows, 2026-11-18 audit).
field_map.permit_type_source: Permit_Type, the county's own permit family (Building, Mechanical, Roofing, Electrical, Plumbing, Gas, Pool/Spa, Demolition, Fire, Sign, Irrigation, Right-of-Way, Tree Removal, and others), with Sub_Type carried in the pull for trade classification only.
field_map.project_description: WorkDescription, the county's own scope text (present on 100% of window permits).
field_map.scope_filter: pull_where_extra excludes six Permit_Type values that authorize no construction — 'Zoning Permits & Information Requests' (60 unscoped window permits; zoning-verification letters), 'Development Review Application' (4), 'Pre-Application Screening' (3), 'Planning, Zoning, and Land Use Applications' (1), 'Public Works Administrative Review' (10), 'Temporary Use Permit' (14) — 92 permits, named and counted here and on the Data Sources page (the San Antonio scope-filter treatment). Kept deliberately: Irrigation Approval, Right-of-Way Connection/Use, and Tree Removal Permit — families authorizing physical work on a site.
field_map.status: Status, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Scoped window statuses are post-issuance lifecycle states (Closed, Issued, Approved, Finaled, Expired, and small residues) — every window record carries an issue date, so they stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: COUNTS-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: the layer's 33 fields carry no cost or valuation field at all (full schema verified 2026-11-18), so there is no figure to validate, compute, or withhold, and none is estimated (the Philadelphia treatment). Alachua publishes counts, trades, and monthly volumes only, stated openly on the hub, the Data Sources page, and llms.txt.

history_range: 218,013 rows at audit (the county's register, 2016 to present in samples); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).
license: Alachua County ArcGIS open data (public access, county-published); attribution: Alachua County, Florida
pull_where_extra: IssueDate <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AND Permit_Type NOT IN ('Zoning Permits & Information Requests','Development Review Application','Pre-Application Screening','Planning, Zoning, and Land Use Applications','Public Works Administrative Review','Temporary Use Permit')
rate_limit: ArcGIS hosted FeatureServer query, 1,000-row pages (the layer's maxRecordCount) with the adapter's 0.4s pacing plus retries; anonymous public tier served the full audit and backfill pulls steadily.
source_name: Alachua County open data — Building Permits (Growth Management)
terms_status: verified-open-2026-11-18: the BuildingPermitsCS layer is published by Alachua County (Growth Management GIS) on the county's official ArcGIS organization with public access, for public reuse; the county's item description states it is updated twice a week. Figures are published 'as reported by Alachua County' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Twice a week per the county's own item description; MEASURED 2026-11-18: layer dataLastEditDate 2026-11-17 and newest IssueDate 2026-11-17. Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the layer's editingInfo.dataLastEditDate under a 96h threshold.
watermark_field: IssueDate + Permit — refresh re-pulls by the IssueDate watermark (same window predicate, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP end bound) and upserts.
